experiment.title: Development-tuned LSEG-33 economic-value rule search
experiment.objective: Test whether a causally formed negative-news pressure rule can add economic value by timing downside risk after costs, beyond both the frozen HAR base and simply holding less exposure.
experiment.evidence_role: exploratory post-hoc model selection with a separate chronological forward test
experiment.retuning_allowed: only inside the complete grid declared below

inputs.source_regime: Reuters LSEG sector-33 only; no mid-cap-22 or FNSPID observations are pooled

chronology.fold_rule: three consecutive equal 152-session blocks; each block is repriced independently with entry and final-liquidation costs
chronology.boundary: the evaluation return path may not enter candidate generation, constraints, ranking or tie-breaking

pressure_family.complete_session_rule: construct a pressure observation only when all 33 firms are present; incomplete development sessions remain missing
normalisers: strictly-prior rolling mean and sample standard deviation
strictly-prior exponentially weighted mean and standard deviation
pressure_family.causality: the current pressure enters the numerator but never its own normalisation baseline

smooth.shape: linear from multiplier 1 at start_z to minimum_multiplier at start_z plus full_cut_distance_z

mapping_family.composition: multiply the frozen unlevered HAR exposure; never exceed the HAR exposure

selection.primary_daily_utility: net_return minus 5 times squared negative net_return
selection.fold_score: annualised mean utility difference versus a constant multiplier with the same mean modifier inside that development fold
selection.selection_score: minimum fold score across the three chronological development folds
eligibility: development mean multiplier is between 0.50 and 0.95
each fold mean net return is no worse than frozen HAR by 1 basis point per session
downside-squared loss is lower than the fold-specific equal-exposure constant in at least two of three folds
primary utility is higher than the fold-specific equal-exposure constant in at least two of three folds
tie_breakers: higher mean fold utility difference versus equal exposure
higher minimum fold utility difference versus HAR

comparators: constant multiplier fixed to the selected rule's mean development multiplier
primary_family: selected overlay minus comparator mean net return
comparator minus selected overlay downside-squared return
comparator minus selected overlay 5 percent expected shortfall
selected overlay minus comparator daily downside utility at risk aversion 5
evaluation.inference: paired circular moving-block bootstrap, 20-session blocks, 9999 replications
evaluation.multiplicity: Benjamini-Hochberg across all eight evaluation tests at q=0.05
descriptive_metrics: ending wealth and loss-day/up-day decomposition per GBP 1 million

claim_boundaries: The earlier and recent LSEG outcomes have both been seen in prior experiments, so this is exploratory rather than pristine confirmation.
Only one complete grid and one deterministic selection rule are reported; all candidates remain in the saved search table.
A positive development score without a positive chronological evaluation is overfit, not economic evidence.
A result versus HAR but not versus the fixed equal-exposure control is exposure reduction, not news timing.
The search does not alter the historical conclusions of Notebooks 72 and 73.
